subject: Biology
summary: Covers hierarchical taxonomic classification: Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum/Division -> Kingdom with specific examples like Homo sapiens, Panthera leo, Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum.
highYieldPoints: Taxonomic categories from lowest (Species) to highest (Kingdom).
As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases.
Mangifera indica: Family Anacardiaceae, Order Sapindales, Class Dicotyledonae, Division Angiospermae.
Homo sapiens: Family Hominidae, Order Primata, Class Mammalia, Phylum Chordata.
potentialMcqThemes: Family vs Order of Housefly (Musca domestica: Family Muscidae, Order Diptera)
Characteristics common at species level vs kingdom level

subject: Biology
summary: Whittaker's 1969 5-kingdom classification based on cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.
highYieldPoints: Monera: Archaebacteria live in extreme environments (halophiles, thermoacidophiles, methanogens with branched lipid chains in cell membrane).
Mycoplasma: completely lack cell wall, smallest living cells, can survive without oxygen.
Chrysophytes: Diatoms have silica walls forming indestructible diatomaceous earth (used in polishing and filtration).
Fungi: Cell walls composed of chitin and polysaccharides; Ascomycetes (conidia exogenously on conidiophores).
Lichens: Symbiotic association between alga (phycobiont, autotrophic) and fungus (mycobiont, heterotrophic). Excellent pollution indicators that do not grow in SO₂ polluted areas.
potentialMcqThemes: Imperfect fungi (Deuteromycetes, e.g. Alternaria, Colletotrichum, Trichoderma)
pyqFrequency: Consistently 3-4 questions every year in NEET

neetTopic: Molecular Basis of Inheritance: DNA Structure & Replication
subject: Biology
summary: Watson-Crick B-DNA double helix model, Chargaff's rule, packaging of DNA helix in nucleosomes, Meselson and Stahl experiment.
highYieldPoints: B-DNA: Pitch is 3.4 nm with roughly 10 base pairs per turn (0.34 nm distance between base pairs).
Nucleosome: 200 bp of DNA helix wrapped around octamer of basic histone proteins (H2A, H2B, H3, H4) with H1 histone holding entry/exit.
Meselson & Stahl (1958): Used heavy nitrogen ¹⁵N and CsCl density gradient centrifugation to prove semi-conservative replication in E. coli.
DNA Polymerase: Synthesizes DNA ONLY in 5' -> 3' direction with high fidelity and proofreading.
potentialMcqThemes: Centrifugation bands after generation I and generation II in Meselson-Stahl experiment
Leading vs Lagging strand (Okazaki fragments joined by DNA ligase)
pyqFrequency: Ultra high yield: 5-7 questions every year in NEET

subject: Chemistry
summary: Explains covalent molecular shapes, valence shell electron pair repulsions, hybridization schemes, and bond dipoles.
highYieldPoints: Repulsion order: lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp.
XeF₄: Steric number 6 (4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs) -> sp³d² hybridization, Square Planar shape.
XeOF₄: Square Pyramidal; XeF₂: Linear (3 equatorial lone pairs).
Bond order formula and magnetic behavior from Molecular Orbital Theory.
potentialMcqThemes: Isoelectronic species with identical shapes (e.g. ClO₃⁻ and SO₃²⁻)
Dipole moments of NH₃ vs NF₃
pyqFrequency: At least 3-4 questions every year in NEET

neetTopic: Current Electricity: Kirchhoff's Laws and Resistors
subject: Physics
summary: Ohm's law, drift velocity, resistivity, emf, series-parallel combinations of cells, and Kirchhoff's loop rules.
highYieldPoints: Drift velocity v_d = eEτ/m; Current I = n A e v_d.
Junction Rule represents Conservation of Charge; Loop Rule represents Conservation of Energy.
Cells in parallel: E_eq = (E₁/r₁ + E₂/r₂) / (1/r₁ + 1/r₂).
Balanced Wheatstone Bridge: P/Q = R/S -> current in central galvanometer arm is zero.
potentialMcqThemes: Stretching of wire by n times or x%
Terminal voltage V = E - Ir (discharging) vs V = E + Ir (charging)
